messages:
jen (support): FYI Acme reported repeated SSE partials + reconnect storms this morning. customer sees chunks stop for ~30-90s, then a reconnect, sometimes duplicate outputs and extra tokens billed. attaching quick logs below.

jen (support): server logs show a bunch of \"write: broken pipe\" and client shows \"ERR_STREAM_RESET\". example: `2026-02-14T09:12:11Z [edge-proxy-7] write failed: EPIPE`

tyler (sre): any fronting CDN/ALB in between? ALBs can coalesce tiny TLS records and drop silence detection.

jen (support): yes — path is client -> customer-proxy -> our edge-proxy -> backend. customer-proxy is an internal proxy with TCP coalescing enabled (they called it "coalesce_small_writes=on").

lucy (eng-runtime): interesting. SSE relies on frequent small writes to keep proxies from idling. If a proxy batches multiple writes into one TLS record or waits for Nagle, the comment ping pattern can be swallowed and the connection appears silent.

omar (eng-ml): do we have timeline/traces for a single session? curious whether token refresh coincides. also: are clients using HTTP/1.1 or HTTP/2? HTT/2 streams behave differently.

jen (support): traced one session: client HTTP/1.1 -> our edge, comments every 30s from server, but proxy coalesced them into an aggregated record every ~2m. client then hit a client-side liveness and reconnected. token refresh happened ~45m later, so not auth in this case.

alia (security): we did see a handful of 401s after reconnection attempts — likely because reconnect client used cached stale token in a race. not ruling out auth race but primary signal is silence + coalescing.

tyler (sre): repro plan? can we reproduce with a small curl chain that simulates coalescing proxy?

jen (support): repro steps I ran: 
1) run a small netcat-based proxy that delays writes by 90s and flushes.
2) curl -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \"https://edge.example/v1/stream\" -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>"
observed client idle -> reconnect loop.

jen (support): curl snippet: `socat TCP-LISTEN:9000,reuseaddr,fork EXEC:'bash -c "sleep 90; cat"' &\ncurl -sv -N http://localhost:9000/ -H 'Accept: text/event-stream'`

lucy (eng-runtime): short-term mitigation ideas: 1) reduce server comment ping to 10s (from 30s) so proxies have less idle time; 2) send an extra \"\n\n\"-terminated noop (force a TLS record) rather than relying on comment-only lines; 3) enable SO_KEEPALIVE on the connection with low interval on our edge. but note proxies may drop/ignore TCP keepalive.

omar (eng-ml): agree. also consider emitting occasional non-comment chunk with a 1-byte payload (e.g., a zero-width space encoded safely) so it can't be stripped by higher layers that filter comments.

tyler (sre): ops/andy, can we flip a config on edge-proxy to set tcp_nodelay / tcp_keepalive_interval=20s for affected pool? Also can we detect TLS-record coalescing in traces (i.e., long server-send gap but single TLS close)?

andy (ops): can do for the pool serving Acme. will test tcp_keepalive=20 + net.ipv4.tcp_keepalive_intvl=20 on the hosts. will report back after a canary.

alia (security): quick ask — if we reduce ping rate, ensure we don't create new abuse vector. rate-limited pings only for active sessions and tied to session ID.

lucy (eng-runtime): longer-term: server should detect write stall (eg write deadline > X) and proactively close and mark session resumable with last-event-id so clients can resume instead of blind reconnect + duplicate billing. also add a header `x-keepalive-probe: v1` to help downstream proxies opt-out of coalescing in future.

jen (support): billing note — duplicates are hitting the ingestion pipeline because reconnects replay same request body in some clients. ops: can we add a dedupe key for recent session tokens to avoid double-billing within 60s?

tyler (sre): for immediate customer communication: ask Acme to route direct to our edge (bypass their proxy) for 24h and see if flapping stops. if it does, confirms proxy coalescing.

jen (support): emailed Acme with repro instructions and a short window (tomorrow 02:00-04:00 UTC) to try bypass. asked for their proxy config snippet. :eyes:

deploy-bot: deploy started by lucy (eng-runtime) for change: reduce-comment-ping -> 10s in staging

lucy (eng-runtime): I'll ship the 10s change to staging and add the noop byte fallback behind a flag. will monitor errors, reconnect rate, and billing deltas.

omar (eng-ml): one more datapoint: add a small metric for "tls-record-batch-size" at the edge so we can quantify coalescing and alert when average > 1 record per 2m.

andy (ops): creating a runbook: immediate steps (tcp_keepalive change, binary noop flag), customer outreach, canary rollout, rollback plan.

jen (support): summary for thread: likely root cause = downstream proxy/TCP/TLS coalescing + comment-only pings being swallowed -> client liveness triggers -> reconnects -> sporadic duplicate billing + auth race. mitigations = reduce ping interval, send forced TLS record/noop bytes, enable tcp keepalive, add dedupe window on billing, improve observability.

tyler (sre): sounds good. follow up: ops, drop me the canary host IDs once applied, I'll watch tracer and error budgets.

jen (support): thanks everyone — will update Acme after staging results.
